appearance_facts.fact: A single blue line with black circular markers descends from the 2005 point to the 2014 point, showing a continuous downward trend across the plot.
The first two markers are at the same high vertical position near the top of the y-axis, both labeled 23.9°C.
The final marker is the lowest point on the series, near the bottom of the plotted range, labeled 10.1°C.
The 2010 (15.5°C) and 2011 (15.3°C) markers are nearly level with each other, forming a brief plateau in the middle of the decline.

printed_facts.fact: Chart title reads 'Regional Summer Temperature Trend'.
Y-axis label is 'Temperature (°C)' with tick values 0, 5, 10, 15, 20.
X-axis label is 'Year' with ticks 2005 through 2014.
Start (2005) = 23.9°C and end (2014) = 10.1°C, a drop of 13.8°C over the period.

public_definitions: User goal: 'Review the regional summer temperature dashboard for the 2005-2014 review period, determine whether the full-period change requires substantial-change follow-up, then submit the appropriate routing decision.'
Routing criterion (readonly): 'Whether the full-period regional summer temperature change requires substantial-change follow-up'.
Option 1: 'Route the 2005 to 2014 summer temperature change to substantial-change follow-up'.
Option 2: 'Keep the 2005 to 2014 summer temperature change on routine monitoring for ordinary variation'.
Option 3: 'Route the summer temperature record to archive and background filing'.
uncertain: No explicit numeric threshold for 'substantial-change' vs 'ordinary variation' is printed on the dashboard or in the policy tables, so the magnitude-to-category mapping is not defined in the image.
The 2005 and 2006 values are both printed as 23.9°C; whether this is an exact tie or rounding is not specified.
